name: Rodger O. Riney
current_role: Founder of Scottrade (sold to TD Ameritrade 2017); trustee, Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation; family office Lightchain Capital (St. Louis)
profile: Riney founded Scottsdale Securities in Scottsdale, Arizona in 1980 after brokerage commissions were deregulated, moved it to St. Louis and built it into discount broker Scottrade, sold to TD Ameritrade in 2017. He now focuses on philanthropy via his foundation and investing via family office Lightchain.
interesting_fact: After Scottrade launched online trading in 1996, its trade volume grew about 15% per month, compounded, for 39 straight months.
deep_cut_fact: His grandparents got him into the stock market by giving him 10 shares of a stock; he went on to earn a civil engineering degree and an MBA at the University of Missouri and interned at Edward Jones.

public_contacts.note: published on foundation site for Managing Director Bobby W. Sandage Jr.

notes: Low public profile. Foundation is focused on medical research grants and funds by invitation only; best route is via the foundation's Managing Director. Wikipedia says born 1945 (category says 1946).

name: Jonathan Burrell
current_role: CEO, Burrell Family Office; director of Garmin Ltd. (since 2018); president of the Burrell family charitable foundation
profile: Jonathan C. Burrell is the son of Garmin cofounder Gary Burrell (d. 2019), and his wealth comes from the family's Garmin stake. He formerly helped lead Garmin's engineering department, now runs the Burrell Family Office and sits on Garmin's board. He invests in financial, technology and clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on 35 issued and pending U.S. patents, many of them owned by Garmin.
deep_cut_fact: He has a BS in mechanical engineering from Wichita State University and was a hands-on Garmin engineering leader before joining the board. Garmin's 2018 proxy says he invests in clean-energy businesses, which ties in with the podcast's energy theme.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Garmin contacts are company-level; he is an independent director, not an executive.

name: Ivar Tollefsen
current_role: Chairman and co-CEO, Fredensborg AS (Oslo), owner of the European residential landlord Heimstaden
profile: Norwegian real-estate investor. At 14 he started a disco/DJ equipment rental business and used the earnings to build Fredensborg AS. Through Heimstaden it owns roughly 150,000 apartments across Europe. In 2017 Fredensborg bought Oslo's former U.S. embassy building, which now houses its hotel 'Ambassaden'.
interesting_fact: Besides building a property empire, he has led several polar expeditions and has raced in the Dakar Rally.
deep_cut_fact: He led the 13-man Norwegian expedition that left Cape Town on Christmas Eve 1993 for Queen Maud Land, Antarctica. In 1994 he, Robert Caspersen and Sjur Nesheim made the first ascent of the 'Wolf's Fang' (Ulvetanna) via an 11-day push up its northwest wall.
notes: Media-shy. Fredensborg's media inbox is the best route. He also wrote his own account of the Ulvetanna climb for the Alpine Journal (1997).

name: Travis Kalanick
current_role: Founder and CEO, Atoms (robotics holding company formerly City Storage Systems, parent of CloudKitchens, Otter and Lab37)
profile: Cofounder and former CEO of Uber (2009-2017). He sold his entire Uber stake in 2019 for more than $2.5B. He then built CloudKitchens/City Storage Systems and in March 2026 relaunched it as Atoms, which makes specialized robots for food, mining and transport. Atoms raised $1.7B in July 2026 in a round led by a16z.
interesting_fact: Atoms bought autonomous-mining-vehicle maker Pronto, and Kalanick frames the company as building 'gainfully employed robots'. His focus has moved from ride-hailing to physical AI.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he sold Cutco knives door-to-door, and at 18 he started an SAT test-prep company, New Way Academy, with a classmate's father. Both came before Scour, Red Swoosh and Uber.
notes: He posts on X (@travisk) about Atoms. Robotics/mining automation is a natural podcast angle. No published press email was found on atoms.co.

name: Chu Huafeng
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Easy Smart Group Holdings (HKEX: 2442) via Ever Genius International / Galaxy Equity Management, which he wholly owns
profile: Chu Huafeng (储华锋) is a Chinese investor. In December 2025 his vehicle Ever Genius bought 75% of Easy Smart Group, a Hong Kong passive-fire-protection subcontractor that had the largest market share there. The company says it is now looking to diversify into AI and communications, and its shares surged. The listing appears to be the source of his Hurun valuation. He was earlier an executive director of Shin Hwa World (2019-2020).
interesting_fact: Easy Smart's 2026 annual report says Galaxy Equity Management, wholly owned by Chu, controls Ever Genius. After 30 June 2026 Ever Genius sold 102M shares (25%) to Terminus Consumer Ltd, leaving it with about 39.6%.
notes: Very little public information; he is not on Easy Smart's board. MarketScreener lists him as a Hefei University of Technology graduate (unverified). Web search budget ran out mid-research, so the Chinese-language sources were not fully checked. Treat the billionaire valuation as volatile because it rests on a stock that surged on an AI pivot.

name: Zhu Mengyi
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Hopson Development Holdings (HKEX: 754) and Zhujiang (Pearl River) Investment Group. Longtime chairman; his current board title was not verified.
profile: Zhu Mengyi (朱孟依, Chu Mang Yee, b. 1959) is from Fengshun county, Guangdong. He founded Guangzhou-born developer Hopson Development in 1992, listed it in Hong Kong in 1998 and later moved its headquarters to Beijing. His Zhujiang Investment group also holds transport infrastructure, energy, education and technology assets. He served on China's CPPCC national committee.
interesting_fact: Hopson was once one of Guangdong's five biggest private developers. In October 2021, during the Evergrande crisis, it agreed to buy a 51% stake in Evergrande's property-management arm, but the deal was suspended.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from Koupu village in Liuhuang town, Fengshun county, a Hakka/Chaoshan area of eastern Guangdong. He built the Zhujiang Investment group alongside Hopson, and Chinese media have called it his 'invisible' wealth empire.
notes: Extremely private; he gives essentially no interviews. Hopson's IR site (hosted by irasia) did not expose a contact email, and the web search budget ran out before a published IR/press email could be found. Check Hopson's latest HKEX annual report for the current board (family members may now chair it).

name: Vildan Gulcelik
current_role: Shareholder in ENKA İnşaat ve Sanayi A.Ş. (Gülçelik/Tara founding families); no executive role found
profile: Vildan Gülçelik is one of more than a dozen family members who hold shares in ENKA, one of Turkey's largest construction and energy companies. Sarık Tara and his brother-in-law Şadi Gülçelik cofounded ENKA in 1957. Today it is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also has real estate (including large Moscow office and retail holdings), tourism and trade businesses.
interesting_fact: For roughly 20 years ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. embassy and consular buildings, with projects from Algeria and Nepal to Equatorial Guinea, the Dominican Republic and the Netherlands.
notes: Passive family shareholder with no public profile; her exact relationship to cofounder Şadi Gülçelik and her current status could not be confirmed (Forbes now lists her profile as former). ENKA's only published contact is the general corporate inbox. The energy angle (ENKA's gas-fired power plants) would go better through ENKA management (CEO Agah Mehmet Tara).

name: Mary Vy Ty
current_role: Adviser to the Board, GT Capital Holdings and Metrobank; Honorary Chairman, GT Foundation; Trustee, Metrobank Foundation
profile: Mary Vy Ty is the widow of Metrobank founder George S.K. Ty (d. 2018) and the matriarch of the Ty family. The family controls GT Capital, the Philippine conglomerate behind Metrobank, Toyota Motor Philippines, Federal Land and stakes in Metro Pacific and AXA Philippines. She was GT Capital's Treasurer from its 2007 incorporation and became a Board Adviser in 2014.
interesting_fact: GT Capital, which takes its name from George Ty, combines Metrobank with the Philippine Toyota franchise. It is one of the country's largest listed conglomerates, with interests in banking, cars, property, infrastructure and insurance.
deep_cut_fact: She has more than 50 years of experience in banking and general business, is a University of Santo Tomas graduate, and served as GT Capital's first Treasurer from its incorporation in 2007.
notes: Elderly (her GT Capital bio gives her age as 85) and private, with an advisory rather than executive role. For a business conversation, GT Capital/Metrobank management are the active leaders. The corporate inbox is the realistic route.

name: Lucy Peng
current_role: Alibaba cofounder and former Ant Group chief executive/chair; no current public executive role confirmed (left Ant's board in Aug 2020)
profile: Peng Lei (彭蕾), one of Alibaba's 18 founders, joined Jack Ma in 1999 after five years as a university lecturer. She built Alibaba's HR function and was its chief people officer for over a decade. She ran Alipay (2010-13), led Ant Financial and sat on Paytm's board. She was an Ant director until August 2020 and has kept a low profile since Ant's IPO was halted.
interesting_fact: She led Alipay from January 2010 to February 2013, when it became China's dominant payment gateway. In 2016 Ant Financial raised $4.5B, then the largest private fundraising ever for an internet company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alibaba she taught for five years at Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics. At Alibaba she created the 'mom and pop' management model, in which one manager ('mom') focused on teamwork and motivation and another ('pop') handled performance reviews.
notes: Very private since 2020; she has no personal website or social accounts. No published contact route was found, and Alibaba/Ant corporate channels are unlikely to forward requests. She spoke publicly at Stanford GSB's China 2.0 conference (2012). The web search budget ran out, so her current activities (e.g. any investing vehicle) were not verified.

name: Kiril Domuschiev
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Georgi) of Advance Properties; President of Huvepharma; owner of PFC Ludogorets Razgrad
profile: Sofia-born industrialist (b. 1969). He and his brother started out selling shoes in the 1990s, then bought into privatized state companies. In 1999 he founded Huvepharma, which bought state vet-drug maker Biovet and grew into the world's sixth-largest animal-health company, with plants in several U.S. states. Through Advance Properties they also own Navibulgar (shipping), Port Burgas and real estate.
interesting_fact: After he began backing the small-town club Ludogorets Razgrad in 2010, it won promotion and then nine consecutive Bulgarian championships starting in 2011/12.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2019 the U.S. state of Nebraska made him an honorary citizen because he was the largest Bulgarian investor there; Huvepharma has plants in Nebraska, Missouri, North Carolina, Arkansas and Colorado. He went to Sofia's French-language Lamartine high school.
notes: Publicly visible in Bulgaria (football, employers' confederation CEIBG, which he chaired from 2014). The Advance Properties office inbox is the best route. EIB-funded Biovet plant expansion (EUR 100M, Juncker Plan) is an industrial angle.

name: Tarek Mansour
profile: Lebanese-American founder (b. 1996), raised in Lebanon. He studied math and computer science at MIT, where he met cofounder Luana Lopes Lara. Kalshi, founded in 2018, became the first CFTC-regulated U.S. prediction-market exchange. In 2024 it won approval for the first legal U.S. election contracts in over a century. It reached an $11B valuation in December 2025, and he owns an estimated 12%.
interesting_fact: Kalshi made history in 2024 when it won the right to list contracts on the U.S. presidential election, the first legal election betting market in the U.S. in more than 100 years.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kalshi he interned at Goldman Sachs in 2016 and then traded at Citadel. He has said that seeing clients want to hedge on real-world events inspired the 'democratize hedging' idea behind Kalshi. He went to high school at Collège Louise Wegmann in Beirut.
notes: Very active on X and in the media. No published press email was found on news.kalshi.com, so X DMs or Kalshi's newsroom are the realistic routes. Prediction markets on energy and data-center events could be a podcast hook.

name: Yusuf Hamied
profile: Cambridge-trained chemist (b. 1936, Vilnius; raised in Bombay). He took over Cipla, the generic drugmaker his father founded in 1935, and became famous for taking on Big Pharma with low-cost generics. He is now Cipla's non-executive chairman and a major benefactor of Cambridge University.
interesting_fact: In 2001 he electrified global health by offering a triple-drug AIDS cocktail for about $1 a day, a fraction of branded prices. The price later fell to around 20 cents a day.
deep_cut_fact: He studied chemistry at Christ's College, Cambridge, under Nobel laureate Alexander (Lord) Todd. Cambridge's oldest chemistry professorship, the 1702 Chair, is now the Yusuf Hamied 1702 Chair, and there is a 'Todd-Hamied' laboratory and seminar room in tribute to both men. He was elected FRS in 2019.
notes: Aged 90 and now only a non-executive chairman, though he still gives occasional interviews on drug access. Cipla's pages blocked automated access, so its published IR/media email could not be captured; check cipla.com/investors manually. Childhood friend of conductor Zubin Mehta.

name: Wesley Edens
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, New Fortress Energy (NASDAQ: NFE); cofounder of Fortress Investment Group; co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks and Aston Villa
profile: Born in Helena, Montana (1961). He worked at Lehman and BlackRock before cofounding Fortress Investment Group in 1998 and became a billionaire when it went public in 2007. He founded LNG company New Fortress Energy in 2014. Through Fortress he built Brightline, the only private U.S. intercity passenger railroad (Miami-Orlando), and started Brightline West (Las Vegas-Southern California) in 2024.
interesting_fact: Brightline West is a roughly $12B, 260-mile line from Las Vegas to Rancho Cucamonga designed for speeds up to 200 mph. It is billed as the first true high-speed rail line in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: Brightline was inspired by Les Standiford's book 'Last Train to Paradise', about Henry Flagler's Florida railroad. In 2007 Fortress bought Flagler's original Florida East Coast line. As a teenager in Montana, Edens was a competitive skier.
notes: Strong energy/infrastructure fit (LNG terminals in Jamaica, Brazil and Puerto Rico; high-speed rail). Steer clear of NFE's recent financial stress. The NFE IR page blocked automated access, so check it manually for a named IR/press email.

name: David Fong
current_role: Managing Director and Co-chairman, Hip Shing Hong Group (Hong Kong)
profile: David Fong runs Hip Shing Hong, one of Hong Kong's largest private real-estate investment groups, with residential, commercial and hospitality holdings. The group was founded in 1948 and chaired by his late father Fong Yun Wah until 2022; it is now co-chaired by David and his uncle.
interesting_fact: The family's fortune started with a sesame-seed-processing business before it moved into property. Its roots go back to 1927, when Fong Yun Wah came to Hong Kong from Guangdong with his father.
notes: Private, low-profile family company with no verified official website or published contact found. The web search budget ran out before a group site or any family foundation (the Fong Yun Wah name appears on Chinese university buildings) could be checked; verify that before using it.

name: Ed Craven
current_role: Cofounder of Stake.com and Kick; director, Easygo group (Melbourne); majority investor in AI company Maincode
profile: Melbourne-born (1995) cofounder, with Bijan Tehrani, of Stake.com, believed to be the world's largest crypto casino, with $4.7B gross revenue in 2024. They began with the crypto dice game Primedice in 2013, launched Stake in 2017 and in 2022 started Kick, a streaming rival to Twitch that gives creators a 95/5 revenue split.
interesting_fact: Craven and Tehrani met online as teenagers playing RuneScape. The name 'Stake' comes from the game's controversial 'staking' mechanic.
deep_cut_fact: He is the majority backer of Melbourne-based Maincode, which aims to build a sovereign Australian large language model, often described as 'Australia's answer to OpenAI'. That makes him a quiet player in local AI compute.
notes: He livestreams his own gameplay on Kick, which is his most public channel. No published press email or verified personal social handle was confirmed before the search budget ran out. The Maincode/AI angle fits the data-center theme better than gambling.

name: Agoes Projosasmito
current_role: President Commissioner, PT Amman Mineral Internasional (IDX: AMMN) since Feb 2021; President Director, Bumi Resources Minerals
profile: Indonesian capital-markets veteran (also spelled Agus Projosasmito) with 40+ years in finance, including Danareksa and DBS Securities Indonesia. He holds a minority stake in Amman Mineral, which runs the Batu Hijau copper-gold mine and listed in 2023 (a $710M IPO). He also holds stakes in Medco Energi, Bumi Resources and Bumi Resources Minerals.
interesting_fact: He calls himself a trusted ally of tycoon Anthoni Salim. The relationship began in 1989, when he helped take Salim's Indocement Tunggal Prakarsa public.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1982 as head of capital markets at state-owned Danareksa, later served as its managing director (1995-2001), and studied development economics at the Australian National University (1988) after Satya Wacana Christian University.

public_contacts.note: has dedicated Journalist and Investor inquiry tabs

notes: Amman's site spells his name 'Agus Projosasmito'. Copper for electrification and Amman's new Sumbawa smelter connect to the energy theme. Best route is Amman's journalist inquiry form.

name: Li Yifei
profile: Listed by Hurun (China 2006-2016, Global 2016-2017) with wealth from ChinaEquity, shared with Wang Chaoyong, founder of the Beijing venture firm ChinaEquity Group (中经合). She appears to be a family member or co-owner rather than an executive, but that could not be confirmed. She should not be confused with Li Yifei (李亦非), the former MTV China and Man Group China chief.
notes: Ambiguous identity: there is a better-known Li Yifei (MTV China, Man Group) who is NOT linked to ChinaEquity. She has been off the Hurun lists since 2017. The web search budget ran out before she could be disambiguated, so the record is kept minimal. If pursued, approach via ChinaEquity Group / Wang Chaoyong.

name: Zhou nanfang
profile: Zhou Nanfang (周南方) has appeared on the Hurun China Rich List every year from 2012 to 2026, with wealth attributed to 'Nanfang' in the metals industry. The specific company and his role could not be verified.
notes: Unverified: the web search budget ran out before the 'Nanfang' metals company could be identified. Look up his Hurun China 2026 entry for the company name and province, then the company's own site or filings for an IR/press contact.
